newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index ends at record high for sixth straight day.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index ends at record high for sixth straight day.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks racked up their sixth record close in a row Wednesday as the market greeted with relief the Federal Reserve's decision to keep interest rates unchanged.
The Dow Jones industrial average was up 8.20 points at 6,274.24, surpassing Tuesday's record finish of 6,266.04.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,289 to 1,109 on moderate volume of 429 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks also set a new high, with a gain of 0.73 of a point at 386.91.

The Dow has risen nearly 250 points over the past seven trading days as Wall Street applauded the election results and bet that the Fed would hold the line on interest rates amid signs that the economy is slowing and inflation is in check.

The central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee ended its meeting at mid-afternoon and left the key federal funds and discount rates unchanged. The funds rate, which commercial banks charge each other for overnight loans, remained at 5.25 percent and the discount rate, which the Fed charges banks for cash, stayed at 5 percent.

The goverment's latest statistics confirmed that inflation was not a problem. The Producer Price Index for October rose 0.4 percent, but the core rate, excluding the volatile food and energy components, fell 0.3 percent -- the sharpest drop since the 0.4 percent decline in October 1994.

"The near-term momentum can carry us higher," said David Shulman, chief equity strategist at Salomon Brothers. "But historically after-election euphoria leads to a market that peaks between Thanksgiving and Christmas."
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond slipped 4/32, lifting its yield up 6.45 percent from Tuesday's eight-month low of 6.44 percent.

Meanwhile, gold prices closed higher following gains in mining stocks and technically-motivated buying. Newmont Mining rose 1-1/2 to 52-1/8, Homestake Mining edged up 1/4 to 16-1/2 and Newmont Gold added 1-3/4 to 50-3/4. Gold closed up 80 cents at $384.20 an ounce on New York's Commodity Exchange.

"It is interesting that gold stocks have been creeping up for the last few days for no reason with inflation under control," said Robert Stovall of Stovall/Twenty-First. Historically, the precious metal has risen in times of inflationary worries.
Among individual stocks, Du Pont lost 2-3/4 to 92-1/2 on speculation that the company would not spin off its Conoco energy unit, traders said. The company declined to comment.

Westinghouse was off 7/8 to 19-3/4 after, as expected, it announced plans to focus on its broadcast assets by splitting in two and spinning off its industrial business. The stock had risen recently in anticipation of the news.
Medex surged eight to 23-1/4 and Furon fell 5/8 to 20-3/8. Furon signed a definitive agreement to merge its unit, FCY Inc., with Medix in a deal valued at $160 million.
Microsoft rose 3-1/4 to 145 on a long-awaited two-for-one stock split. Dell Computer surged 3-3/4 to 92-3/8 after reporting quarterly results that far exceeded analysts' estimates.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 4.19 points to 1,260.72.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks was up 1.57 at 731.13. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.67 to 584.31. The average NYSE share was up 8 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,083.104 up 15.475 or 0.22 percent.
